I need to write a eulogy for my grandfather that I've been living with and taking care of for several years. We're not going to have a preacher speak, but rather those that are willing will take turns.

Since my hard drive is dying and I haven't even opened the packaging on my new hard drive to try and assemble another PC, I figured I'd post it here as I write it because if I save it to my dying disc I'd probably end up losing it.

--

Papaw was the most gentle man that I ever knew. He was so gentle, that for every kids' birthday, he'd give them a birthday spanking.. one wack for every year old they were, and one to grow on. It was a fun joke because everyone knew he'd never hurt anyone. Getting a spanking from Papaw on your birthday was something you had to go do.. you were missing out of you didn't make it. I still remember my last one when I was 12.

He used to build tiny scale houses out of wood, cardboard, cellophane and fabric pieces. He even made tiny couches and chairs and the lights worked on the little fireplace mantle. I loved watching him while he worked. He could take a flat piece of cardboard, make a few delicate slices and bends, coat it in glue and then fabric.. and turn basically nothing it into a little couch for the house.

Papaw loved the deck that he built. He finished it in the mid 80s and in July of 86 and we had our first 4th of July on top of it. Shooting off fireworks from way up there was a lot of fun. They used to put a lot more black powder in fireworks, back then. We had a roman candle ball ricochet into someone's window, across the street.. and one of the jumping jacks that Granny tossed bounced up onto the hood of a police car and burned a black ring into it.

He loved that deck, not for what it could do for him, but what it did for his family.. It allowed Granny to get into and out of the car while it was raining without being soaked.. and the grand-kids loved playing on top of it.. and Vick sunbathed up there and Eddie shot arrows at targets down in the yard. He even had a gap at the back door just so Granny could see the sky from inside the laundry room.

Once his eyesight got to where he wasn't able to craft, he took to driving. As soon as Granny first stirred in the morning, he'd ask and see if she was ready to get in the car and go out on the road. He really didn't care where he went, he just loved to drive. They'd be gone from as soon as he could get her out the door until about five or six in the afternoon.. and then sometimes he'd ask her if she'd like to go around the block again, once they'd got back home.

Papaw worked as a mechanic. He had tools that I never knew the purpose of.. or even the names of.. and by the time I thought to ask him about them, he couldn't remember. It really seemed like an honor to me that, a few years ago, he came up to me and asked me to change his oil and his spark plugs and flush his radiator. A man that had worked on vehicles to feed his family was entrusting me with work on his car.

I never really knew how to work on cars.. and I had even taken my own car to Fairmount to have my oil changed.. but if Papaw asked me to do something I was going to at least try. He hovered over me and watched from every angle while I slowly figured it out. I still remember the two hours spent trying not to spit and cuss while fighting the spark plugs on the back side of that engine.. From that day I've gone from learning how to change my own oil to changing my brakes and rotors and I'll be replacing my fuel filter and vacuum lines in the near future. I wouldn't have the ability to do any of that if wasn't for Papaw. I'm thankful for the time that I had and I'll make sure to keep feeding the birds in the front yard that he loved to sit and watch.
may he find peace wherever he is now.
